Subject: SIG follow-up: provenance / prompt retention details

Sergio,

Thanks for the SIG submission earlier this week. Security has a couple of focused asks so we can close out our review:

1) Canonical flow for prompts and model calls — what is persisted vs ephemeral (KV cache, prefix caching, request/response logs)?
2) Retention windows and redaction policy for prompt logs and KV cache snapshots. Any sample log with redaction markers would help.
3) Do you ever use customer prompts or outputs for model training? If so, what is the opt-in flow and controls?
4) Evidence: an internal playbook/diagram and a packet (attestation + sample logs) we can share with InfoSec.

Can you send a short one-page playbook plus sample artifacts? We have an exec SIG review on Monday.

Thanks,

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers first, then attachments and next steps below.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Prompts and responses are written to transient request logs for 30 days by default, searchable for debugging and quality.
- KV cache and prefix caches are held in-memory on the inference node and are not persisted to durable storage by default; occasional snapshots for debugging are captured only with customers' explicit permission and are redacted.
- We do not use customer prompts/responses to train models by default for hosted customers. Training-on-customer-data is a separately contracted opt-in governed by a DPA addendum and documented consent flow.

Attachments I am including: redwood_sig_response_playbook.pdf (one-page playbook), sample_redaction_log.txt (sanitized example), and DPA opt-in flow diagram (dpp-opt-in-flow.png).

What I will do next:
- Soojin will add technical detail on KV handling and snapshot controls.
- Dev will confirm legal-safe wording for the DPA opt-in clause.
- Marissa will coordinate a short call if you want to walk through the packet before Monday.

If you need these artifacts in a ZIP or S3 transfer, say the word and we will provision a time-limited link.

Alex / Sergio — adding the technical specifics so your reviewers can see the engineering controls. Short bullets followed by operational notes.

Persistence model and caches:
- Request/response logs: written to encrypted object storage (customer-segregated buckets) and retained 30 days by default. Retention configurable via account settings; can be set to 0 days (no retention) at onboarding.
- KV / prefix cache: in-memory only (GPU/node RAM). No automatic disk persistence.
- Snapshotting: node-level snapshots (for reproducing issues) require an explicit support ticket and customer approval. Snapshots are redacted and stored encrypted for up to 7 days unless extended, per customer consent.

Redaction and de-identification:
- Our standard redaction pipeline removes 1) direct identifiers (emails, SSNs), 2) structured PHI patterns, and 3) tokens matched by customer-provided deny-lists. We annotate logs with redaction markers like [REDACTED_EMAIL]. Sample attached: sample_redaction_log.txt.

Training and model updates:
- By default, hosted inference does NOT incorporate customer prompts/responses into model training.
- Customer-requested training (fine-tune or continual) is opt-in only: requires a signed DPA addendum + model training SLA, and the training dataset is kept in a segregated training bucket with MFA-protected access.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers control whether their data is used for any benchmarking or training; we never use Private deployment data for public model updates without explicit written consent.

Cryptography & key management:
- All at-rest artifacts are encrypted with customer-unique KMS keys (or Redwood-managed keys if customer prefers). Secrets used by workers are stored in HSM-backed vaults in our production accounts.

Operational evidence we can share now:
- One-page provenance playbook (attached)
- Sanitized log sample (attached)
- Short runbook describing snapshot request process (included in the playbook)

I can provide a short sequence diagram if that helps your SIG reviewers.

— Soojin
